title: Brand, position and target: choose where you will win

say: Brand, position and target: choose where you will win.
This is the video for module one of Brand Strategy and Positioning.
People often say brand when they mean the logo. Your brand is what people think and feel when they hear the business name.

panel.heading: A brand is not the logo
items: Brand: what people think and feel
Position: the place you choose to own

say: Your brand identity is the set of tools you control: the name, logo, colours, packaging, photos and the way you write.

panel.heading: A brand is not the logo
items: Brand: what people think and feel
Position: the place you choose to own

say: Your position is the specific place you want to own in the customer's mind, compared with her other choices. You cannot print a position on a flyer. You earn it by repeating one clear idea, in words and actions.

panel.heading: A brand is not the logo
items: Brand: what people think and feel
Position: the place you choose to own

say: A brand strategy answers five questions. First, the target. Not everybody who eats, but, for example, office admins in Port Harcourt who order snacks for meetings.

panel.heading: Five decisions to write down
items: Target: who exactly are we for?
Frame of reference: compared with what?

say: Second, what will she compare us with? Third, why choose us? Quality and good service is what every competitor says. Delivered hot, on the agreed time, with a proper invoice, is a real difference.

panel.heading: Five decisions to write down
items: Target: who exactly are we for?
Frame of reference: compared with what?

say: Fourth, the proof, like an on-time delivery log. Fifth, the personality: calm, punctual, polite.
A strong answer is narrow enough that some customers say, this is not for me. That is a good sign.

panel.heading: Five decisions to write down
items: Target: who exactly are we for?
Frame of reference: compared with what?

say: When customers see no real difference, the only thing left to compare is price.

Ada has no clear position. She sells at 75,000 naira, a profit of 15,000. A customer says another vendor is cheaper, so she gives 10 percent off, 7,500 naira. Her profit falls to 7,500. One discount halved it, because discounts come straight out of profit.

Bisi positions herself for office admins: hot delivery at the agreed time, a proper invoice, and a contact who answers. She sells at 95,000 and earns 35,000 per tray. Admins rarely ask her for a discount.

First, match the basics, the points of parity, so you are not rejected. Parity gets you on the shortlist. Difference wins the choice. A good point of difference is relevant: the target actually cares.

cards.d: The target segment actually cares about it.
Competitors do not already own it.
You can keep it true every week, not just at launch.

say: It is distinctive: competitors do not already own it.

say: And it is deliverable, every week. A broken promise damages the brand faster than having no promise. Build your position only on things you can prove.

say: A positioning statement is an internal sentence, not an advert. For example, Hauwa runs a tutoring centre in Abuja. Her first draft said: we offer quality education for all children.

panel.heading: Hauwa writes a positioning statement
items: Who: have children facing BECE or WAEC
Because: a progress report every Friday

say: Her records show most paying parents both work full time, with children preparing for BECE or WAEC. So: for working parents in Gwarinpa whose children face these exams, Hauwa's Study Hub is an exam-focused tutoring centre.

panel.heading: Hauwa writes a positioning statement
items: Who: have children facing BECE or WAEC
Because: a progress report every Friday

say: Unlike home lesson teachers, she sends a written progress report every Friday, so parents always know where their child stands.
Now run the swap test. Put a competitor's name in. Quality tutoring with caring teachers fails, because every centre could say it. Hauwa's passes.

panel.heading: Hauwa writes a positioning statement
items: Who: have children facing BECE or WAEC
Because: a progress report every Friday
panel.rule: Swap test: put a competitor's name in. Still true? Not different.

say: Positioning only works once you know whose mind you are winning. For example, Zainab sells shea butter from near Tamale. She scores three segments from 1 to 5 on size, willingness to pay, reachability, and fit, with weights that add up to 100 percent.

panel.heading: Zainab scores three segments
items: Primary A; C kept for later

say: Mothers buying for babies score 3.85. Wedding favour planners score 3.30. Diaspora natural hair buyers score 3.50.

panel.heading: Zainab scores three segments
items: Primary A; C kept for later

say: So she positions first for mothers, and keeps diaspora buyers for later, once she has a reliable shipping partner.
Because this segment is about babies and skin, she never claims the product treats or cures anything. She positions on clean processing and gentle use, which she can show.

panel.heading: Zainab scores three segments
items: Primary A; C kept for later
panel.rule: Weights must add up to 100%. Choose one primary segment.

say: Check your segment against five tests. Measurable, substantial, reachable, different and actionable. If it fails one, it is an idea, not a target.
Reachable matters most here. Can you reach them cheaply, through WhatsApp groups, church or mosque networks, or market associations?

panel.heading: Five tests of a useful segment
items: Reachable: you can get to them

say: To remember. Your brand lives in the customer's mind. Decide your target, frame, difference, proof and personality. Without a difference, customers compare price only.
Make your difference relevant, distinctive and deliverable. And segment, target, then position.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Brand lives in the customer's mind

say: Now choose one business for this whole course. Ask five customers for three words they think of. Draft three positioning statements. And score your segments to choose one primary target.
